newsitem.title: USA: Chicago mayor proposes $395 mln football stadium.
newsitem.headline: Chicago mayor proposes $395 mln football stadium.

text.p: Chicago Mayor Richard Daley Friday unveiled a plan to spend $395 million to effectively rebuild the city's professional football stadium, Soldier Field, and add a retractable roof.

The mayor's plan calls for the issuance of $160 million of revenue bonds by the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority. The city and state authority would use revenues from existing lodging, restaurant, and rental car taxes collected in the Chicago area to pay off the bonds.

Another $60 million of bonds would be issued, possibly by a new bonding authority, according to Walter Knorr, Chicago's chief financial officer. Those bonds would be paid off with football revenues and would be taxable, Knorr added.
The Chicago Bears football team would be responsible for coming up with $175 million of the funding through their own financing and the sale of personal seat licenses.
